subject: moon-phases
title: Why Does the Moon Change Shape?
summary: The Moon never really changes shape. Our view of its sunny side does.

keys.answer: It is sunlight bouncing off the Moon. The Moon makes no light of its own.

options.text: Sunlight bouncing off the Moon
The Moon glowing on its own
Light from stars shining on it

keys.prompt: Why does the Moon seem to change shape?
keys.answer: As the Moon travels around Earth, we see more or less of its sunny half.

options.text: We see more or less of its sunny half
Earth's shadow covers part of it
The Moon gets bigger and smaller

keys.prompt: About how long does the Moon take to go through all its phases?
keys.answer: About 29 and a half days, from one new Moon to the next.

cards.title: A shape-shifting Moon?
cards.text: Look at the Moon tonight. Then look again in two weeks. It might go from a thin sliver to a big, round ball! Did the Moon really change?

cards.question: What do you think makes the Moon look like it changes shape?

options.text: Earth's shadow covers part of it
We see different amounts of its sunny side
Clouds in space hide part of it

cards.reveal: We see different amounts of the Moon's sunny side as it travels around Earth. The Moon's shape never changes.

cards.title: The Moon has no light
cards.text: The Moon does not make its own light. Moonlight is really sunlight bouncing off the Moon. The Sun always lights up the half of the Moon that faces it. The other half is dark.
cards.example: Shine a lamp on a ball in a dark room. One side glows. The other side stays dark.

cards.title: Our view changes
cards.text: The Moon travels around Earth. As it moves, we see more or less of its sunny half. The Moon never really changes shape. Only our view of it changes!

why.q: Why can't Earth's shadow be the reason?
why.a: Earth's shadow does fall on the Moon sometimes. That is a lunar eclipse, and it does not happen every month. Phases happen every month.

cards.title: A growing Moon
cards.text: At new Moon, the dark side faces us, so we can't see the Moon. Then a thin sliver shows up. That is a crescent. It grows into a half circle, then a full Moon. Growing is called waxing.
cards.example: In the U.S., a growing crescent is lit on the right side.

cards.title: A shrinking Moon
cards.text: After the full Moon, the bright part shrinks. That is called waning. It goes back to a half circle, then a thin crescent lit on the left. Then it is new Moon again. The whole trip takes about 29 and a half days.

cards.question: People long ago used the Moon to keep track of time. Why do you think the Moon worked well for that?
nudges: What can everyone see, wherever they live?
How often do the phases repeat?

options.text: Sunlight bouncing off the Moon
options.why: Yes! The Moon reflects the Sun's light.

options.text: The Moon glows on its own
options.why: The Moon makes no light of its own. Without the Sun, it would be dark.

options.text: Lights from Earth's cities
options.why: Moonlight comes from the Sun, not from Earth.

questions.q: Why does the Moon look like it changes shape?

options.text: We see different amounts of its sunny half
options.why: Right. Our view changes as the Moon goes around Earth.

options.text: Earth's shadow covers part of it every night
options.why: Earth's shadow only covers the Moon in a lunar eclipse, and that is not every month.

options.text: The Moon really gets bigger and smaller
options.why: The Moon stays the same size and shape. Only our view changes.

questions.q: What is a waxing Moon doing?

options.text: Growing
options.why: Yes! Waxing means the bright part is getting bigger.

options.text: Shrinking
options.why: That is waning. Waxing is the opposite.

options.text: Staying the same
options.why: The bright part is changing. Waxing means it is growing.

sources.title: What Are the Moon's Phases?
sources.supports: The Moon makes no light of its own; moonlight is reflected sunlight; the Sun always lights the half facing it; our view changes as the Moon orbits; the eight phases; waxing means growing and waning means shrinking; in the Northern Hemisphere the waxing crescent is lit on the right and the waning crescent on the left; about 29.5 days from new moon to new moon.

sources.title: Lunar phase
sources.supports: Phases are not caused by Earth's shadow; the lit fraction is (1 − cos θ)/2 where θ is the elongation; 27.3-day orbit vs 29.5-day phase cycle because of Earth's orbit (13.4 orbits but 12.4 passages a year); eclipses need new or full Moon and the 5° tilt usually prevents them; around 59% of the surface imaged from the ground thanks to libration; 12 lunar months are 10 or 11 days short of a solar year, so lunar calendars drift and lunisolar calendars add a 13th month.

sources.title: What Is an Eclipse?
sources.supports: During a lunar eclipse, Earth's shadow covers the full Moon; lunar eclipses don't happen every month because the Moon's path is tilted.
